page: Google Cloud Platform n4d-standard-48 is a general-purpose virtual machine built on the x86_64 architecture. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs spanning 24 physical cores and 48 execution threads on an AMD EPYC 9B45 processor. Memory allocation stands at 192 GB of system RAM, maintaining a standard balanced ratio of 4 GB per vCPU. Hardware instruction extensions include AVX-512 vector support (with VNNI and BF16), AES, and SHA_NI cryptographic accelerators. The instance contains no bundled local storage and no dedicated hardware GPUs, relying instead on network-attached block storage for disk persistence.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong computational capabilities, particularly in single-core and multi-core processing. In Geekbench testing, the instance achieved a single-core score of 2,578 and a multi-core score of 23,419, ranking both in the top tier. Raw compute throughput tested with stress-ng produced 3,444.29 points in single-core and 82,542.49 in multi-core metrics. Memory caching registers 4,967.9 GB/sec for small 16 KB read blocks, though large 256 MB uncached transfers moderate to 143.14 GB/sec for reads and 80.53 GB/sec for writes. The processor shows high single-threaded performance during compression routines, producing 37.83 GB/sec in gzip compression and 16.7 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression.

From an efficiency perspective, the n4d-standard-48 offers a balanced distribution of execution threads and memory capacity, avoiding the premiums associated with GPU coprocessors or specialized high-memory configurations. However, workloads requiring extreme memory streaming bandwidth or non-volatile local disk scratch space face architectural tradeoffs due to the reliance on external storage networks. The hardware configuration makes this server suited for mid-tier relational databases, Redis caching clusters running high volumes of operations, static web serving infrastructure, enterprise Clang compilation pipelines, and CPU-based lightweight AI inference.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4d-standard-48 is a general-purpose virtual machine equipped with 48 dedicated vCPUs across 24 physical cores, powered by an AMD EPYC 9B45 x86_64 processor. The configuration provides 192 GB of system memory, matching a standard 4 GB per core density, but excludes local NVMe storage and dedicated GPUs. Performance benchmarks place the instance in the top tier for single-core and multi-core processing, with high throughput in image manipulation, text parsing, and data compression. While uncached large-block memory bandwidth remains in the middle range, the server delivers strong efficiency for memory-to-core balanced workloads. It is suitable for enterprise microservices, Redis caching setups, relational database backends, Clang compilation, and CPU-driven small model machine learning inference.
